title: Gas station
statement: Station i on a circular route gives gas[i] and it costs cost[i] to drive to station i + 1. Starting with an empty tank, return the station index from which you can complete the circuit, or −1. (If a solution exists it is unique.)
hints: If total gas < total cost, it's impossible; otherwise a start exists.
If you start at s and run dry at j, no station between s and j can be a valid start either.

solution.explanation: Two claims, each worth proving aloud: (1) total gas ≥ total cost ⇒ some start works (start just after the minimum of the prefix sums); (2) if starting at s you first run dry arriving at j + 1, then every start in (s, j] also fails, because you reached each of them with a non-negative tank and still failed. So jump the candidate to j + 1. One pass. The proof is the answer: without it the code looks like a guess.
solution.python:
def can_complete_circuit(gas, cost):
    if sum(gas) < sum(cost): return -1
    start = tank = 0
    for i in range(len(gas)):
        tank += gas[i] - cost[i]
        if tank < 0: start = i + 1; tank = 0
    return start
